precepts.text: Not slothful in business: this is talking about God's business. Cuz if it was the white man's business, you wouldn't be slothful, cuz you got to eat, you got to have a place to live. But fervent in spirit, on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
The nobleman gave the pounds “that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.” The trading is going out teaching the word. It is business: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.”

This is talking about God's business. If it were the white man's business, you wouldn't be slothful, because you've got to eat, you've got to have a place to live. But in God's business people get slothful. Be fervent in spirit, on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

The first servant's pound gained ten pounds and the second's gained five, and they were rewarded with cities. The servant who was slothful in the Lord's business laid his pound up in a napkin and gained nothing.

precepts.text: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another. Not slothful in business: not lazy concerning God's work. Fervent in spirit: be on fire in your spirit, serving the Lord.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is the unfeigned love of the brethren, real and not put on.

“Not slothful in business”: not lazy concerning God's work. “fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit. “serving the Lord.”

This is the opposite of walking feignedly. The feigned brother came in on fire and now has to be yelled at and forced; the hireling looked back from the plough. The one Ezra asks God to remember, one “which according to thy will have known thy fear”, is kindly affectioned to the brethren, not slothful in God's business, and on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

precepts.text: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. That's if possible. We've seen some instances on the news where it was impossible; you had to throw hands to some people, because some people are irate, some people are unreasonable.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” That's if possible. As much as lies in you, you live peaceably, and that includes the Edomite the law says you shall not abhor, for he is thy brother.

But we've seen some instances on the news where it was impossible; you had to throw hands with some people, because some people are irate and some people are unreasonable. Paul did not say peace at any cost; he said as much as lieth in you.

So the law of Deuteronomy 23:7 is not a command to be harmless. It is a command not to carry hatred and seek harm. We live peaceably as far as it depends on us, and we are not the ones who start it.

precepts.text: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another. You know that offends white folks: we were on a quest reading scriptures among ourselves, and these white people, they hate that. The other nations hate that thing.
precepts.point: Therefore, brethren, stand fast: stand firm in his truth. And hold the traditions which ye have been taught: hold the traditions of God's laws as you've been taught, whether by word, face to face, or our epistles.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is how the chosen are to walk with each other, those God “hath from the beginning chosen” to salvation “through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth.”

You know that offends white folks. We were on a quest reading scriptures among ourselves, and these white people hate that. The other nations hate that thing: our people gathered together, loving one another, preferring one another in honour.

That is what it means to “stand fast, and hold the traditions which ye have been taught.” Stand firm in his truth, and hold the traditions of God’s laws as you have been taught them, whether by word, face to face, or by the epistles. The law says be kindly affectioned one towards another, and that brotherly love among ourselves is part of holding fast to the truth while the rest of the world believes the lie.

precepts.text: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. That is: if it be possible.
precepts.point: For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto. Blessed are the peacemakers, but peace does not always work with some people; some spirits are grimy, and at the end of the day they don't want peace with you.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Onias sought peace, going to the king seeking the good of all rather than to accuse his countrymen. That is one of his attributes, and Paul gives the rule: “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.”

Notice the words: if it be possible. As much as lies in you, you live peaceably. But it is not always possible. Onias “saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto.” Simon was causing insurrections in Jerusalem, and Onias wanted the king to look into it.

Blessed are the peacemakers, and live peaceably if at all possible, but peace doesn’t always work with some people. Some spirits are grimy, and at the end of the day they don’t want peace with you. They want you dead. Onias did everything that lay in him; the rest he took to the king.

precepts.text: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another. That is our hearts being knit together as one man. Honor is a word we have never been taught as a race, as a people. Definition read in class: honor refers to the moral principle of integrity, fairness, and respectability; the term encompasses both a personal ethos and the public esteem in which a person is held; character and integrity, high moral standards, honesty, and a guiding code of conduct. We try to teach the commandments as a guiding code of conduct, and they call it hate speech. In honour preferring one another: you will hear our people say they prefer another race over their own, because we have never learned honor. Story told in class: a store owner shot a young black boy in the back and got off, and our people went right back to shop at those stores. That is preferring other races to your own race.
precepts.point: The acknowledgment of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ: that goes back to the chapter before.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love”: that is our hearts being knit together as one man. Then: “in honour preferring one another”. That right there is our problem.

Carter G. Woodson told it: a black store sells ice, and a white man opens an ice store right next door. Guess where black people go to buy ice? The white man's, because they say the white man's ice is colder. In Chicago it's the same with the barber shops: I'm going to the Chinese barber shop because they give better haircuts. You hear black women and black men say, I prefer the white man, I prefer being with the white woman. Why? Because we have never learned honor.

Ask black men and women to explain honor and you get the pimps and the hoochie mamas trying to explain it; they have no honor. We have never been taught honor as a race, as a people. Honor refers to the moral principle of integrity, fairness and respectability; it takes in both a personal ethos and the public esteem in which a person is held: character and integrity, high moral standards, honesty, and a guiding code of conduct. Blacks and Latinos do not understand high moral standards: why can't I show my cleavage, my stomach, the crack of my booty? We try to teach the commandments as a guiding code of conduct, why cover up, why put down the guns, and they call it hate speech. They only do that with our race.

The law says, “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself”. The children of your people are the children of your race, not the Chinese, not the white man, not the Arabs. Yet we will love any other race before we love each other. A Chinese man shot a little black boy in the back and killed him; they said he had a gun and found no gun, and he got off. And our people went right back to shop at the Chinese stores, as long as they could get the fake hair, the press-on nails and the makeup. That is preferring other races to your own race, when God says, in honour prefer one another.

precepts.text: Be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind. I knew I was in the right place when I was surrounded by men and women that decided to put everything behind them and do what God said, whether it was fashionable or not. At one point fringes were not fashionable; at one point modest apparel for the women was called oppression. We are not oppressing them; we are giving them what God said.
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
Rather than roll with those that had no vision, the choice was to stand with those that decided to turn against the ways of the world: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

It was clear this was the right place when surrounded by men and women who decided to put everything else behind them and not be conformed to this present world, who decided, we are going to do what God said.

It may not be fashionable. At one point fringes weren't fashionable; now everybody's mama wants fringes. At one point it wasn't fashionable for women to be in a dress, fully covered in modest apparel. They said, y'all are oppressing them women. No, we are not oppressing them; we are giving them what God said.

That is building on the right foundation. Those who do his commandments have a good understanding, and that is why you are here as well.

precepts.text: For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office. The mind does not have the same function as the hand; the hand does not have the same function as the foot; but they all need each other. The body cannot function with all hands; if everybody comes in trying to be the feet, what happens? Disorder.
precepts.point: Each and every one of you has been gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation. For those who think you are insignificant: God called you in here, so you had better apply your gifts and talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” God organizes the body, and God is who made us great. We are at the forefront, considered the vanguard, because God appointed us to be; if we move any differently than that, God will remove us and put somebody else there. Each of us was gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation.

Romans says the same: “For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”. Why do the members not have the same office? The heart and the brain function in different ways, but they come together to make the body function as one. The mind does not have the same function as the hand, and the hand does not have the same function as the foot. Every member functions, but they all need each other.

The body could not function with all hands or all elbows. If everybody comes in trying to be the hands, or everybody trying to be the feet, what will happen? Disorder. Everybody cannot be the head; everybody cannot be the shoulders. Everybody has their function.

So for those who think you are insignificant, just a regular Joe: God called you in here, and you have a mission and a purpose. You had better apply your gifts and your talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God. And preparing as a nation means more than food and water: we need lawyers, doctors, nurses, farmers. Go to school; master any skill, any trade, and bring that mastery back to benefit your nation.

precepts.text: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. We are all expendable and can be replaced if we do not put something into this truth. When members begin to think they are more important than another, dysfunction comes into the body, and members start treating other offices like they are less important. Where would we be without security? Unsafe. Without the brothers and sisters that clean? Infested. Without the kitchen? Hungry. There is not one office we can say is more important; they all play a part. Even with leadership: a deacon is not better than you. I have to keep the commandments and believe on Christ just like you. If you start to think you are better because of your office, this body is going to suffer. Respect the sisters changing diapers; respect the brother folding flyers, who in his tenure has probably put a million flyers into rotation in the earth.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
God has given us different gifts and different offices but the same mission. So Paul says, “to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” We are all expendable; we can all be replaced if we don't put something into this truth.

What happens when someone thinks more highly than he ought? Just because you're the knuckle, the one who keeps us safe, you think you're better than everybody else. When members begin to think they are more important than another, dysfunction comes into the body, and members start treating other offices as less important.

Where would we be without security? Unsafe. Without the brothers and sisters who clean the toilets, the kitchen and the floors? Infested with roaches and mice. Without the kitchen? Hungry as hell; some single brothers look forward to the Sabbath because they get a real meal and not the peanut butter and jelly they're used to. The Lord brought all these administrations together so we can function. Not one is more important; they all play a part.

Even leadership. A deacon is not better than you; he could die tomorrow and be the devil. He has to keep the commandments and believe on Christ just like you. At the gas company nobody says, oh, that's Deacon; they say, nigga, I had to come shut your stuff off for you to come see me. No one cares. If you start to think you're better because of your office, this body will suffer. Respect the sisters changing diapers; respect the brother folding flyers, who in his tenure has probably put a million flyers into the earth, and it may have been you who got one.

precepts.text: When you come into this truth you are supposed to transform the way you think; the scriptures are supposed to be inside you now. That you may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God: to prove means you are not ignorant. It is the ability to process, to identify, to differentiate. Your antennas are up now. In the church you were ignorant, just walking along the line doing what everybody was doing: Christmas, birthdays, Mother's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, never asking why. Now everything has to make sense: what does the scripture say, where is that in the Bible?
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
To be not ignorant, Paul tells the Romans: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. When you come into this truth you are supposed to transform the way you think. The scriptures are supposed to be inside you now, and you have to apply them.

And why? “that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” To prove means you are not ignorant. It is the ability to process, to identify, to differentiate. Your antennas are up now, and you will not be ignorant in anything any longer.

You were ignorant in the church. You were dumb as hell, stupid, knowing nothing, just walking along the line doing what everybody was doing: it is Christmas time, it is somebody's birthday, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, and never asking why. But now you are different. Now it has to make sense: what does the scripture say, where is that in the Bible? That is proving what is acceptable unto the Most High God, his perfect will.

precepts.text: Whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; or ministry, let us wait on our ministry; or he that teacheth, on teaching. Everybody staying in their lane, working within the gift and skill set you have been given, not trying to force things that are not you. At camp, you cannot put the brother that is 105 pounds at the front sentry; he might be the fire teacher, or real good on flyers, but the wind will carry him off and we will not have a front sentry. When you operate outside your character, things get messy, and the person that should be in that position cannot operate the way the body needs, so we lack in different areas. Years ago a certain brother was put over the bills; one Sabbath the lights were off, and we learned that day he is not the one to put over the bills. We found where he belongs, and he is operating within his place now. Everybody does not belong everywhere.
precepts.point: All these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. God has divided to every man as he wanted. Everyone has received something. New brothers and sisters, you are trying to discover what the Lord wants you to do here, because you woke up in this time period for a reason. What are you bringing to the table? How are you going to benefit your people and carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same: this is not just about the brothers, it is about a nation.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
“Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”. These are the different gifts, administrations and operations. Whatever gift you have been given, if it is prophecy, prophesy with everything you have; whatever the Lord gave you, that is what you give.

“Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching”. Everybody stays in their lane. You work within the gift and skill set you have been given, and you do not try to force things that are not you. Size is not everything, but at camp you cannot put the brother who is 105 pounds at the front sentry. He might be the fire teacher, or real good on flyers, but if the wind blows it will carry him away and we will not have a front sentry.

When you are outside of your character, things get messy. If you pretend to be something you are not, you may be put in that position, and the person who should be there cannot operate the way the body needs, and we lack in different areas. Years ago a certain brother was put over the bills; one Sabbath the lights were off at the school. We learned that day he is not the one to put over the bills. We found where he belongs, and he is operating within his place now. Everybody does not belong everywhere.

“Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.” Everyone in their office, in their proper position. That is what Paul means when he says the one Spirit is “dividing to every man severally as he will.”

precepts.text: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord. That's the proof that the business is God's business.
precepts.point: The famine was over all the face of the earth, and all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn. That's what it's like when you have a plan, a solution. Joseph didn't sit around and wait for the dearth; the Most High showed him what was coming, and he made moves of preparation. This is how we have to be in IUIC.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Proverbs says “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings,” and Paul shows which business that is: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.” That is the proof. The business is God's business, serving the Lord, and you must not be slothful when it comes to it.

That is the business Joseph was about. He served faithfully in Potiphar's house and in the prison, he gave God the credit before Pharaoh, and he was fervent, not asleep, when the answer was needed. He is the diligent man who stood before kings.

So don't be over there asleep in the things of God. Be fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, and God will set you before kings and not before mean men, as he did Joseph.

precepts.text: If ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: when we obey the elements of the flesh and make the bottle an outlet, the end of that road is always death. But if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live; for as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.
precepts.point: Captain's teaching: it is not a sin to drink, but when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good, which is God's laws.

note.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

precepts.why:
It is not a sin to drink. But when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation; it is not to be used in that manner. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome these things.

“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die”. To live after the flesh is to obey the elements of the flesh: going to the bottle and making that the outlet. The end of that road is always death, just as Habakkuk 2:12 shows that there is always an evil road, and at the end of it you find death.

“but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live”. That is where we are. The drinking problem in this land is a quarter trillion dollars, but the commandments fix all of that.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” That is how we are to be. So we should not be overcome with that evil; we have to overcome that evil with good, and the good is God's laws.

precepts.text: Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart and cheerfulness of the mind; but wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind. The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element the Lord created has its function and purpose, but if you abuse it you cannot be useful to the nation. It goes for food as well; that is why they put the fast food across the street from more fast food in our neighborhoods. They are depending on you to fall into that destruction.
precepts.point: Captain's teaching: it is not a sin to drink, but when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good, which is God's laws.

note.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

precepts.why:
“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind”. Measurably. The wine is not the sin; the measure is the key. “But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind”. That is the key point: bitterness of the mind.

The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element on the earth was created by the Lord, and it has its function and its purpose. But if you use it and abuse it, you cannot be useful for the nation.

It is the same with alcoholism as it is with food, which the Bishop has been bringing out: all of it has a balance, and if you overuse it you fall. Our oppressors are depending on us to lose that balance. That is why you have the KFCs across the street from Domino's, and the liquor stores in our neighborhoods: they are depending on you to fall into that destruction, that chaos, that confusion.

Nobody out there is drinking measurably or sociably; it is used to drown out reality, and it will kill you. So overcoming evil with good means holding the balance the Most High set in every element, and not letting the bottle become the outlet.

precepts.text: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good. Do not let this world destroy your faith; with the good of these commandments and the faith of Christ, knowing who you are, you overcome that evil with the good of this Bible.
precepts.point: Not slothful in business: our business is that we are called by God to magnify the law and increase our faith. Fervent in spirit; serving the Lord by doing the work and helping your people. Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; distributing to the necessity of saints. What better life to live than to help your people?

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
The first step is study, pray and apply: do your research, and then turn from sin. Then we have to learn how to turn all of this evil and mischief into righteousness, from the power of Satan to God, from darkness unto light. Romans 12 lays out the steps: “Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.” Come home, family.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another”: looking out for each other and honoring one another within our marriages, our relationships and our nation. “Not slothful in business”: our business is that we are called by God to magnify the law and increase our faith. “Fervent in spirit; serving the Lord”: doing the work and helping your people. “Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Distributing to the necessity of saints”. What better life to live than to help your people?

And the chapter ends with the sum of it: “Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.” Do not let this world destroy your faith.

How do we overcome? With the good of these commandments and the faith of Christ, and knowing who you are. You overcome that evil with the good of this Bible. Love without dissimulation, brotherly love, fervency, patience and prayer are the good that overcomes the evil around us.

precepts.text: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
precepts.point: And be not conformed to this world: why? Because of who rules over this world. Do not take the mind of Cain. But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind: after Christ; that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Paul says, “be not conformed to this world”, because of who rules over this world: the white man. Don't have the mind of the Edomite, the mind of Cain. Instead, “be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”, after Christ. Just before, Ephesians told us, “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” That is what we have to do. But how do we really go about doing it?

David asks the same question: “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way?” How can we cleanse our ways? “by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

The renewing of the mind comes by the word. We have to take heed according to the word, and that is how the bitter spirit, the leaven of Cain and Esau, is cleansed out, so that we may prove “what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

precepts.text: Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile: that is the fake talk because you are bitter; and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.
precepts.point: And be not conformed to this world: why? Because of who rules over this world. Do not take the mind of Cain. But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind: after Christ; that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Peter shows what the renewing of the mind looks like: “Wherefore laying aside all malice.” Lay aside all malice, family: all malice, all leaven. “and all guile”: that is the fake talk, because you are bitter. “and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings.” We have to lay these things aside.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” We have to be born again in Christ like newborn babes. The sincere milk of the word is the thing we have to desire, and it is what makes us grow.

This is Romans 12:2 at work. Being conformed to this world is carrying the mind of Cain and Esau: the malice, the guile, the envy and the evil speaking of the bitter spirit. Being transformed is laying all of that aside and feeding on the word until the mind is renewed after Christ.

precepts.text: Lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves: we hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then do not do it. That is the man beholding his natural face in a glass who goeth his way and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was. We do not want that: we want to examine ourselves and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit.
precepts.point: And be not conformed to this world: why? Because of who rules over this world. Do not take the mind of Cain. But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind: after Christ; that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
James tells us what to put off and what to take in: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The word received with meekness is what saves the soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” We have to be doers of the word, family. We hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then we don't do it.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” When you read the scriptures, you see yourself in them. But after you read them, you go your way and don't really address the matter.

We don't want to do that. We want to examine ourselves, look to the scriptures and say: Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit. I'm bitter toward my wife, I'm bitter toward the leadership, I'm bitter toward my brother. We have to confess that thing and pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is being transformed by the renewing of the mind, and not conformed to this world.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice: every prophet who goes out to teach does, as John on Patmos and James beheaded did; we are the true martyrs.
precepts.point: Be thou faithful unto death and I will give thee a crown of life: nothing they can take can make you betray eternal life, because there is no resurrection for them. He that hath an ear, let him hear; you have to keep the commandments to understand it, and he that overcometh is not hurt of the second death, the death over your soul.

note.label: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.why:
“Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” This is what we are going to sacrifice to get what is actually ours: eternal life, the kingdom of heaven.

Paul says it: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Every time these prophets go out to teach the word, they are presenting their bodies a living sacrifice. All the prophets in the Bible did it, even unto death. John was banished to the isle of Patmos; James was beheaded. They were martyred because they understood the mission, and you brothers and sisters have to understand the mission. We are the true martyrs.

Many read “be thou faithful unto death” and do not understand it. You have to put yourself there and say: there is nothing these nations can do to me, nothing you can take from me, to make me turn and betray my eternal life. There is no resurrection for them.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear”: you have to be spiritual, keeping the commandments, to understand it. “He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death”, the death the Lord has power over, the death over your soul.

precepts.text: Be not conformed to this world but transformed by the renewing of your mind. New creatures in Christ; if you feel Satan raising his head and the old man coming back, do everything to deaden that spirit.
precepts.point: We look not at the things which are seen, which are temporal, but at the things not seen, which are eternal. America influences the whole world in music and culture, but this power will fall; the kingdom we cannot see yet lasts forever. Stack your bricks and do not be a situational Israelite.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“the things which are not seen are eternal” We do not see the kingdom yet, but it will last forever. So we have to stack our bricks, and we cannot be situational Israelites. We have to be in the spirit and move in the spirit, knowing our eternal home awaits us. It is a spiritual battle, a spiritual war.

“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. We have to change by the renewing of our minds, because we are now new creatures in Christ. The mindset has to change.

Those things that used to trip us up so often and so easily in the world, in this day and age, cannot keep doing it. If you feel Satan raising up his head against you, if you feel that old man coming back, you have to do any and everything to deaden that spirit. Now ain't the time for that.

That is what it means to look not at the things which are seen. The world presses its pop culture and pleasures on us, but a mind renewed stays fixed on the eternal kingdom rather than conforming to a power that is about to fall.

precepts.text: That they might see that they themselves are beasts: as the one dieth, so dieth the other, and a man hath no preeminence above a beast. The wisest man said it.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Paul says “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly”. If God is revealing himself to you, and he doesn't deal with everybody, you had better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God.

Solomon shows why: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” We are all beasts. Although we may be the sons and daughters of God, at the same time we are still beasts in his eyes.

“For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other”. The lion, the bug that has no value in the eyes of God and just serves the purpose it was created for: we die just like them. “yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.” This is Solomon, the wisest man ever to walk the earth besides Jesus the Christ, saying you have no preeminence above a beast.

So who are you to think you are better than that, to reject what God has written and do as thou wilt? Break it down to its lowest form, and we perish just like everything else. That is where humbleness comes in. We came here and we are going to leave here, so apply these excellent things to your life before you go back to your Maker.

precepts.text: Ye are gods, children of the Most High, but ye shall die like men. We rank higher in God's creation but perish like everything else.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” That's why we say it: the Israelites are gods upon this earth, children of the Most High.

But read on: “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” We die just like men, just like the beasts of Ecclesiastes 3. In the grand scheme of things, we have no more power over death than the animals do. Are we higher up on the ladder of God's creation? Sure we are. But we perish just like everything else he has created.

That is exactly why a man must not think of himself more highly than he ought to think. Being called gods and children of the Most High is no ground for pride, because the same ones called gods fall like the princes. Think soberly: the one who knows he will die like men humbles himself before the God who made him.

precepts.text: The days of our years are threescore years and ten, and if by reason of strength fourscore, yet is their strength labour and sorrow, and we fly away. Take care of the temple so God may be merciful with the eighty.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten”: seventy years is what we have. “and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years”: if God is merciful, we might get eighty years out of this body. You know the Bible is a true book: you get to hitting around forty and you say, damn, David was right.

That's why Captain Gideon did the class about working out, not drinking sodas and calcifying the bones, eating once a day and taking good care of yourself, so God can be merciful: he did real good with that temple I gave him; let me give him eighty years.

“yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” We fly away means the spirit goes back to its Creator. That is the one day a man is going to fly: when he gets up out of this body.

And even eighty years is nothing to God. Peter says one day with the Lord is as a thousand years; by that measure a whole human lifetime is less than two hours in God's eyes, and it could be even less. Your life is but a vapor. So how do you look down on others and think so highly of yourself? Think soberly, and humble yourself.

precepts.text: All flesh waxeth old as a garment, for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death; as the green leaves, one generation cometh to an end and another is born.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death.” That is what we just read in David: seventy, maybe eighty years. That is the covenant God pronounced from the beginning: thou shalt die the death.

“As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born.” That is why we have kids. You watch them grow up, and you say, man, I'm getting old. You know the covenant God pronounced upon all flesh, and you are about to cross it too.

“Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.” That is the covenant: thou shalt die the death, thus saith the Lord. Everything a man builds goes with him. So there is no room to think of yourself more highly than you ought; think soberly, knowing the covenant is coming for you like every other leaf on the tree.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ. Sin entered when Adam hearkened to his wife, and death with it; the gift comes after we pass through that covenant, and pride will keep us from it.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Why do we die? We try to break it down so the new people coming into the faith can put the puzzle together: “For the wages of sin is death”. That is why the covenant, thou shalt die the death, passed upon all of us. When Adam listened to his wife Eve and consented to the idolatry she brought to him, sin came into the world, and when sin came, death came with it.

“but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That is what we get in the repentance. But we still have to go through the covenant of all flesh. You can't receive the gift of eternal life while you are still in the flesh; flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven. We have to pass through that covenant.

And one thing we had better make sure we don't have on us when we leave this body is pride. That will keep us out of it for sure. That is why Paul says not to think of yourself more highly than you ought: the one who dies like the beasts receives the gift only through Christ, and only if he goes to his grave humble.

precepts.text: Prophesy according to the proportion of faith. If Deuteronomy 28 is as far as your gift goes, do that and do not reach past it. But do something.
precepts.point: Ten gained ten cities and five gained five, and the one who did nothing loses his one city to the brother with ten.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God; that is the offering of him that has no gold nor silver.
precepts.point: The badgers' skins settle a confusion: the Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin; brush your hair, brothers.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
The offering for the tabernacle was “gold, and silver, and brass, And blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair, And rams’ skins dyed red, and badgers’ skins, and shittim wood, Oil for the light, spices for anointing oil, and for sweet incense, Onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod, and in the breastplate.” Thank the Most High he requires no gold and silver now, for half of us would have nothing to give. Under the new covenant the offering is this: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” The body presented a living sacrifice is the offering of him that has no gold nor silver.

The badgers’ skins in this offering settle a confusion. The Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin. Brush your hair, brothers.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
precepts.point: In our captivity, with no Levitical priesthood and no temple, keeping the commandments is the offering and the reasonable service: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, and we present our bodies a living sacrifice, sacrificing the lusts and pleasures of the flesh to follow the footsteps of Christ. And Ezekiel 20 shows that when Israel is brought back through the wilderness, offerings will be required again in the holy mountain.

note.label: Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings

precepts.why:
With no temple, the sacrifice is ourselves: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.”

The bullock was killed and laid on the fire to be “a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord.” We present our bodies a living sacrifice, sacrificing the lusts and pleasures of the flesh to follow the footsteps of Christ. Keeping the commandments is the reasonable service.

precepts.text: Be not conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.
precepts.point: Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.”

Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind. “be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” Not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

The same word stands for us. When the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
precepts.point: If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
All the sacrifices of the seventh month were for the set feasts of the Lord, and they came “beside your vows, and your freewill offerings”, which carried sacrifices of their own. The feast days were wrapped in offerings from the sabbath to the solemn assemblies, and that is why Paul wrote, let no man judge you in meat or in drink.

What is left for us is better. Paul beseeches the brethren “by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” The bullocks and rams are gone; the body is the sacrifice now.

Keeping the feast days is how that body is presented. Telling your employer months ahead that you need the day of atonement or the tabernacles off, and helping supply the feasts, is presenting the body a living sacrifice. That is the reasonable service the set feasts ask of us today.

precepts.text: Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord: do not avenge yourself, for revenge only brings judgment on you.
precepts.point: Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.” This is why Christ said resist not evil where the law said eye for eye and tooth for tooth.

Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head. The wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him: give place unto wrath, and he will repay.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God; the animal no longer suffices, the sacrifice is your body.
precepts.point: Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them.” At the time it was spoken, that encompassed everything, the law of sacrifice included. It applies to us today as well, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals: it is our bodies.

Paul says it: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” The animal no longer suffices; the sacrifice is your body. And the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord, so our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. That is how confirming all the words of this law to do them reaches into our day.

precepts.text: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men; that is the walk commanded now.
precepts.point: Understand the frame: we live peaceably with all men and lay hands on no one; we do not incite or condone any violence, and if we hear of any we report it. The day of Psalms 137 has not yet come; it belongs to the return of the Lord, so chill out and relax, none of that is for now.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” That is the walk commanded now.

Understand the frame: we live peaceably with all men and lay hands on no one. We do not incite or condone any violence. The war from generation to generation is fought now by casting down the imagination of the adversary, and the day of Psalms 137 belongs to the return of the Lord.

precepts.text: In so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head; David's faithful service under a hateful king did exactly that.
precepts.point: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them; everybody knew he was the one really putting his life on the line and doing the work, even though he had no throne.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
“Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.”

David's faithful service under a hateful king did exactly that. “David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and the Lord was with him. Wherefore when Saul saw that he behaved himself very wisely, he was afraid of him.” David's continued righteousness heaped coals of fire on Saul. When your righteousness makes the wicked afraid, that is how you know you are in the spirit.

precepts.text: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men; we are at peace with all men now.
precepts.point: Our forefathers were aggressive toward the nations in that time period, but that is not the time we are in now. The word tells us to be at peace with all men; we do not break the laws of the land, for this is at present a spiritual battle and not a physical one.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
David took the strong hold of Zion from the Jebusites. They thought to put a stipulation on him, “Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither”, thinking he could not come in at all. They did not reckon with a man who had already slain his ten thousands. “Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion.” When the scripture says nevertheless, it means the thing will be done regardless of what stands against it.

Our forefathers were aggressive toward the nations in that time period. David was a man after God's own heart who would not let any nation stand in the way of the Lord's people, and “the Lord God of hosts was with him.”

But that is not the time we are in now. “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” We are at peace with all men. We do not break the laws of the land, for this is at present a spiritual battle and not a physical one.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. This means the dietary laws are not done away, the dress code is not done away, and we still keep the ceremonial laws when we come back into the knowledge of who we are.
precepts.point: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord. The sacrifice of righteousness today is keeping the law and presenting your body a living sacrifice.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
The sacrifice of righteousness today is also our own body: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Presenting your body a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable, is the sacrifice David speaks of.

That means the dietary laws are not done away, the dress code is not done away, and we still keep the ceremonial laws when we come back into the knowledge of who we are. Keeping the law in the body is our reasonable service.

precepts.text: Be not conformed to this world but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, to prove the good and acceptable will of God.
precepts.point: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. We must understand what we read; this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” This is what David means by a clean heart and a right spirit: a renewing of the mind. It is the same thing Nicodemus was asking about when he wanted to know how a man can be born again.

You are transformed by the renewing of your mind, and by it you prove what the good and acceptable and perfect will of God is. Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart, and do not be conformed to this world.

precepts.text: Avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath; vengeance is mine, I will repay, saith the Lord.
precepts.point: He shall reward evil unto mine enemies; cut them off in thy truth. Vengeance belongs to the Most High, not to us.

note.label: Psalm 54: Save Me by Thy Name

precepts.why: “He shall reward evil unto mine enemies: cut them off in thy truth.” David leaves it to the Most High. “Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.” Vengeance belongs to the Most High, not to us. He rewards evil to the enemies and cuts them off; we give place unto wrath and let him repay.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
precepts.point: What shall I render unto the Lord for all His benefits toward me? The apostle Paul answered that question.

note.label: Psalm 116: I Love the Lord Because He Hath Heard My Voice

precepts.why:
“What shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits toward me?” The apostle Paul answered that question: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.”

For the Lord dealing bountifully with us, delivering our soul from death, our eyes from tears and our feet from falling, what we render is ourselves: our bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable unto God. It is our reasonable service.

precepts.text: Vengeance is the Most High's and he will repay, the assurance Solomon gives against successful wicked men.
precepts.point: Do not worry about the wicked that are successful and all they are doing, because there is a God and that God will have his vengeance. This is why the scriptures say vengeance is his and he will repay.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

precepts.why:
“Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.”

Solomon says when you see the oppression of the poor and the perverting of judgment and justice in a province, “marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.” Do not worry about the wicked that are successful and all they are doing, because there is a God and that God will have his vengeance. Vengeance is his and he will repay; that is the assurance against successful wicked men.

precepts.text: The Most High dealt to every man the measure of faith, so the disciples' understanding grew in increments.
precepts.point: "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
Even after all of this they asked, “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” That shows the Holy Ghost was not yet fully given.

It is given in measures: “God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” Every man is dealt a measure of faith that he has to grow in. In Christ there was no measure, but the disciples knew only so much at that time, and their understanding grew in increments.
